slides.title: Generator Expressions vs List Comprehensions
slides.prompt: Generator expressions provide a compact syntax for creating generators using parenthesis `()` instead of square brackets `[]`. They yield values one by one without creating the entire sequence in memory.
slides.codeSnippet:
import sys

list_comp = [x * 2 for x in range(10000)]
gen_exp   = (x * 2 for x in range(10000))

print(sys.getsizeof(list_comp)) # ~85000 bytes
print(sys.getsizeof(gen_exp))   # ~200 bytes

slides.title: Reusability of Generator Expressions
slides.prompt: Can a generator expression be iterated over multiple times without recreation?
options: No, once fully consumed, subsequent iterations will produce no items
Yes, generator expressions auto-rewind upon second iteration
Yes, but only if passed into a for-loop
slides.correctAnswer: No, once fully consumed, subsequent iterations will produce no items

slides.title: Filtering inside Generator Expression
slides.prompt: Fill in the conditional keyword used to filter elements inside a generator expression.
slides.codeSnippet: evens = (x for x in range(10) ___ x % 2 == 0)

slides.title: When to Choose List Comprehension Over Generator
slides.prompt: When is a list comprehension preferable to a generator expression?
options: When you need to iterate over the dataset multiple times or require random indexing access [i]
When dealing with infinite data streams
When memory consumption must be strictly minimized
When pipeline performance needs lazily computed results
slides.correctAnswer: When you need to iterate over the dataset multiple times or require random indexing access [i]
